correctness.rationale: For x_ij∈{0,1}, open selected neighbors at (i,j) are exactly r_i+c_j−2x_ij. If some row has two selected cells their two columns must be fully selected, and every other column nonempty. At 6,7,8,9-cell thresholds these constraints classify optima: n2 all cells; n3 two full columns and one double; n4 two full and same-row singles; n>=5 three full or one full+three doubles with missing-row permutation; additionally n5 two full+three same-row singles. Counts: 1,9,18,160, and binom(n,3)+n(n−1)(n−2)(n−3) for n>=6; gamma values 6,8,8,9. Independent direct adjacency-bitmask enumeration of all subsets of sizes 1 through the proposed optimum for n2..6 (187573 examined) agreed. Full proof uses row-rigidity, not bounded enumeration.
